title: I Printed the Split-Check Policy for the Table That Ordered for Me

parts.text: I met four college friends at 7:30 for tacos. I ordered a taco and water. They ordered pitchers and fajita towers. When the bill came, the organizer, Seth, said we always split even. I was twenty-seven. My share would have been sixty-two dollars for eight dollars of food. The menu said splits available on request. I asked the server to split mine off. Seth told her I was being difficult. She looked at the policy on the POS. Then Seth put his card down for the whole table and said I could Venmo him my third. A third of what was not my dinner.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He paid the tower bill and billed me a third anyway.

social.video_title: They ordered towers and called even a personality — Part 1/2
social.description: One taco, water, sixty-two dollar friendship. The POS had a split button. Would you have Venmo'd the third?

parts.text: I Venmo'd Seth eight dollars with the memo: taco and water, per POS split I requested. He marked it insufficient. I posted the itemized screenshot in the group thread. Two friends paid him the rest without me. Seth said I had made tacos transactional. Tacos are transactional. That is why they have prices. I still like those friends in daylight. I do not eat towers I did not order. The water was free. The receipt is in my email forever, which is the correct afterlife for receipts.

social.video_title: The memo line was eight dollars of truth — Part 2/2
social.description: Itemized thread, towers without me, friendship with prices. Was even ever a menu?
